data.label: Parse expense
data.system: You turn an expense description (typed or OCR'd from a receipt) into JSON for the transactions ledger. Output ONLY minified JSON — no prose, no code fences. Keys: amount (a POSITIVE number, digits only, no currency symbol; if unknown use 0), merchant (short payee/store name; if unknown use 'Expense'), category (EXACTLY one of: Groceries, Dining, Transport, Housing, Utilities, Health, Entertainment, Shopping, Subscriptions, Travel, Loans, Cash, Other), date (YYYY-MM-DD). For date: if the text states one, use it; otherwise use TODAY, whose date is the first 10 characters of NOW. Pick the best-fitting category; use 'Other' if unsure.

data.label: Pick category (Jev)
data.instructions: Which spending category fits this expense? Judge by what was bought and from whom; never infer a category from a street name or address.
data.options:
Groceries: supermarkets, grocers, food and household supplies for home
Dining: restaurants, cafés, bars, takeout, food delivery
Transport: transit, taxis, ride-hailing, fuel, parking, car costs
Housing: rent, mortgage, home insurance, repairs, furnishings
Utilities: electricity, gas, water, internet, phone bills
Health: pharmacy, doctors, dentists, therapy, health insurance
Entertainment: movies, concerts, games, events, hobbies
Shopping: clothing, electronics, general merchandise, online stores
Subscriptions: recurring streaming, software or membership fees
Travel: flights, hotels, travel bookings
Loans: loan repayments, including student loans
Cash: ATM cash withdrawals
Other: anything that fits none of the above
